state_summary.problem: Canceling the new-run confirmation from practice can return to a practice screen whose context flag was already cleared.
state_summary.expected: Cancel returns to the same isolated practice context without normal-run statistics or run events.
observed: Code inspection: practice-play-button sets training=false before confirmNew with backScreen practice.
Code inspection: back sets the screen to practice without restoring the training flag.
Practice-complete start also clears training before confirmation; returning to its result uses the normal result branch.
unknown: Compiled browser impact has not yet been measured.
state_summary.operation: Practice → 本番を遊ぶ → new-run confirmation → cancel

codex_independent_judgment.rationale: Initial handlers clear training before confirmation. Cancel restores only screen, so the practice UI/result is interpreted as a normal context: controls lose isolation, hint/undo can mutate the saved normal run assist counters, and completion enters the normal result branch. This violates the explicit separate-practice requirement and can mislead users about the practice outcome. Current handlers defer training reset until accepted start, retaining isolated practice on cancel. Browser cancellation and completing practice after cancel remain necessary acceptance checks.

actual_next_action.description: Read initial practice start handlers, cancel/back routing, result branch, assist controls and current handlers. Verified current handlers preserve training when showing confirmation. No browser test performed in this finding review.

state_summary.problem: Replacing a saved unfinished run after a reload reports its end before restoring its saved run identifier.
state_summary.expected: An explicit reset ends the saved run using its original telemetry identifier before starting the new run.
observed: Code inspection: title sets active=false and offers new-game confirmation for a saved unfinished run.
Code inspection: start sets active=true, rebuilds saved board and calls end(reset), without calling restoreRun.
resumeSaved and portal explicitly restoreRun; the replacement path currently does not.
unknown: Root integration of run telemetry context has not yet been compiled into this worktree.
state_summary.operation: Reload unfinished CPU game → New game → Confirm

codex_independent_judgment.rationale: Reload creates an analytics context with run null. Initial replacement path reconstructs the board then calls end(reset) without restoring saved.runId, whereas resume and portal restore it. Therefore reset is not attributed to the original saved run. Gameplay replacement is still available, so this specific defect is not independently judged a major player-facing release risk; it still needs correction to meet continuation telemetry requirements. Current start restores saved.runId before end(reset). Root restoreRun validates UUID and sets context run/phase without emitting another run_start. Frozen integration must verify the actual reset event keeps the prior ID and new run_start creates a new one.

actual_next_action.description: Compared initial replacement/resume/portal paths with current start and root telemetry get/restore methods plus analytics context creation. No external API or browser measurement performed.

state_summary.problem: After the selected column becomes full, keyboard selection still targets its disabled button.
state_summary.expected: After each turn, a keyboard user can focus a legal column and continue using arrows and Enter.
observed: Code inspection: render disables a full column but leaves selectedColumn unchanged.
Code inspection: focusColumn selects by selectedColumn and calls focus even when the button is disabled.
Arrow-key handling is attached to the board, so focus outside its descendants does not reach that handler.
unknown: Compiled keyboard behavior after a full-column CPU sequence remains unmeasured.
state_summary.operation: Fill the selected column → CPU response → keyboard next turn

codex_independent_judgment.rationale: Initial render leaves the selected full column disabled with tabindex0 and all remaining legal columns tabindex-1. focusColumn tries the disabled selected button. CPU-turn render can move focus outside the board, so Arrow/Enter do not reach board handler and Tab cannot regain a legal tabindex0 column. This blocks the specified keyboard interaction in an otherwise playable match. Current render replaces a full selected column with the first legal column before generating tabindex and CPU completion explicitly focuses it. Compiled CPU and same-device fill-column sequences still need measurement.

actual_next_action.description: Read initial and frozen current render, focusColumn, CPU completion and board keydown routing. Confirmed current legal-column reassignment occurs before tabindex/disabled rendering. No browser operation performed; root owns current compiled probe.
